chapter.title: Generator Test Friday
chapter.sub: Three skipped tests, twelve minutes of battery, and a transfer switch that wouldn't transfer.

items.text: SEASON 11 · EPISODE 5 · DRAFT · CASE-059  The Brennock County EOC and the generator yard · Maya, Hektor (facilities manager) and Director Oduya · Level L6 · Mastery support (reference only — choose the tool and say why)  The generator hasn’t carried the room in three months. Everyone assumes it would. Nobody has asked the transfer switch.  ⚑ RV-182: the generator, the transfer switch and the UPS are facilities’ — nobody else touches them. RV-183: figures illustrative. Some choices run on a clock — and some depend on your loadout.

items.title: Generator Test Friday
items.stakes: Three generator tests skipped in flood season, because the test gives the room a blip.
items.reward: A chain proven under load — and a fault found on a Friday instead of in a flood.

objectives.text: Find what the UPS really holds

items.rumor: A test is a fault found on your schedule.

items.alt: The generator yard: the generator enclosure behind a fence, the transfer switch cabinet marked ATS and FACILITIES; Hektor, in an orange vest, points at the generator; Maya with a notebook.

bubbles.text: Every test, someone loses a call and blames me. So we stopped.
Then let's make it a test nobody loses anything in.

items.caption: Three blank Fridays.

lines.text: Every test, someone loses a call and blames me.
Then let's make it a test nobody loses anything in.

items.prompt: 10:10. Three load tests skipped in flood season. What do you ask for?
items.risk: Finding the fault in a real outage.
timeout: The fourth test is skipped too.

hints.text: Who can test it — and what should you know before they do?

options.label: Press the ATS test button yourself while you're here
options.consequence: Not yours — and a test nobody planned.
options.fail: The generator and the transfer switch are facilities'.

options.label: Ask facilities and the director for a load test this Friday afternoon, outside any activation — users told, a load-shed plan ready — and read the UPS's state with Hektor first
options.result: Hektor reads the UPS with you: 9 kW on batteries at about 60%.
options.consequence: The owner's test, planned like an exercise, starting from the numbers.

options.label: Leave it — the generator ran fine two years ago
options.result: Nobody hears a blip. Nobody learns anything.
options.consequence: Trusts a run from two years and three loads ago.

options.label: Ask for a bigger UPS
options.result: A bigger battery in front of an untested switch.

items.title: Twelve minutes, not thirty.
items.body: The UPS was sized, five years ago, for thirty minutes at six kilowatts. The room now draws nine: more screens, more desks, a space heater under every other chair. Its batteries report 61% health, three menus deep. Usable energy about 2.0 kWh, 90% efficient, into nine kilowatts: twelve minutes. With a load-shed plan — break room, printers, spare workstations and half the wall off — eighteen.
items.label: Test: what did the label promise — and what's left?

items.caption: The label was five years old.

items.title: ‘battery health: 61%’
items.body: The UPS's front panel, three menus deep: ‘Battery health: 61% · replace recommended.’ The warning had been on for eleven months. The menu it lived in was three levels down.

items.prompt: The UPS holds about twelve minutes. Friday at 14:00 is approved. How does the test run?
items.risk: A test that fails in a way that hurts people.

hints.text: What would make this a test that nobody loses anything in?

options.label: Cancel it until there are new batteries
options.result: Then nobody finds out whether the switch works.
options.consequence: Protects the test from finding anything.

options.label: Every desk told by Wednesday; the load-shed plan rehearsed at 13:50; facilities' manual-transfer procedure ready; the director's go at 13:59; you watch the room, facilities run the power
options.result: At 14:00 the mains go. The generator is up in nine seconds. The ATS doesn't move. The shed room rides the UPS; facilities transfer by hand at 14:07.
options.consequence: An exercise, not a surprise — with every owner in place.

options.label: Run it unannounced to see how the room really reacts
options.result: Two agencies lose calls; one loses a map it hadn't saved.
options.consequence: A drill nobody agreed to, at their expense.

options.label: Run it at 03:00 when the room is empty
options.result: The room is never empty in flood season — and at 03:00 the load isn't the real one.
options.consequence: A test of a different room.

items.title: Generators upstairs, fuel downstairs
items.body: In late October 2012 a hurricane's storm surge flooded the basements of several big hospitals in the north-eastern United States. Some had generators on upper floors that had passed their tests — but their fuel pumps were in the basements. Patients were carried down dark stairwells. A test of one part isn't a test of the chain.

items.text: Act II — “The test that found the fault”

items.title: The test that found the fault.
items.body: 14:00:00, mains off. The shed room goes quiet — the break room, the printers, half the wall — and keeps working on the UPS. 14:00:09, the generator is running. And the automatic transfer switch doesn't move. Hektor's team opens the cabinet by their procedure: a failed control relay. At 14:07 they transfer by hand. In a real outage, in a flood, the room would have run on its batteries, beside a running generator, until it went dark.
items.label: Test: how close — and whose hands?

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #106 · AVERY'S LENS  Test the whole chain, on purpose, on a calendar  A generator that has never carried the room under load is a hope. Test monthly with the owner, users told and a load-shed plan ready — so the fault is found on a Friday afternoon, not in a flood.  Three skipped tests hid a dead transfer switch and a UPS that could hold the room for twelve minutes, not thirty.

items.alt: The generator yard, the generator running with exhaust rising; Hektor, grim, holds a failed relay in his gloved hand; Director Oduya beside the fence.

bubbles.text: Dead relay. If this had been a real outage, it'd have been my switch that dropped your room.
It wasn't. It was Friday at two, with your procedure ready.

items.prompt: If the switch had failed in a real outage, it'd have been my switch.

options.label: “And today it failed on your schedule, with your procedure ready. That's the job done right.”
options.reply: First Friday of every month, then. And I'll tell them why.

options.label: “It was your switch.”
options.reply: I know. That's why I'm saying it.

items.prompt: The ATS relay failed; the batteries are at 60%. What happens after Friday?
items.risk: The next flood arriving before the fix.
timeout: The relay stays dead over the weekend.

hints.text: What has to be true before you trust the chain again?

items.note: Draft decision (DR-S11E05). Option B needs Budget at LIMITED or better.

options.label: Stop testing — it only causes problems
options.result: The next dead relay waits for a real outage.
options.consequence: Punishes the test for finding a fault.

options.label: Facilities replace the relay and retest under load on Monday; the director funds new batteries; a load test on the first Friday of every month, with the load-shed plan rehearsed each time
options.result: Relay replaced Monday; the retest transfers in ten seconds. Batteries ordered. The first Friday of every month is on every desk's calendar.

options.label: Replace the relay and schedule monthly tests; batteries ‘next budget year’
options.result: The switch works. The room has twelve minutes, not thirty, until next year.
options.consequence: The best you can do without the budget — and it leaves the minutes short.

options.label: Leave the ATS on manual permanently so it can't fail
options.result: Every outage now waits for someone from facilities to arrive.
options.consequence: Turns an automatic safety into a person on call.

items.alt: The backup-power sheet after the repair: a green bar for new batteries and the room shed to 6 kW — 30 minutes; the retest timeline: mains off 14:00:00, generator up 14:00:09, the ATS transferring at 14:00:10.
items.caption: Proven under load.

items.title: Jun · Jul · Aug: ‘postponed — complaints’
items.body: Facilities' generator test log: ‘May — pass. June — postponed (complaints). July — postponed (complaints). August — postponed (activation).’ Three blanks where a dead relay was waiting.

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  A UPS, a generator and a transfer switch are one chain, and only a load test proves it. Runtime shrinks quietly as loads grow and batteries age (t = E × η ÷ P) — plan what to shed. Run the test on the owner’s calendar, with users told and the procedure ready, so the fault is found on a Friday afternoon, not in a flood. Power is facilities’; nobody else touches it.
